<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL" id="Definitions_SupplierOnboarding" targetNamespace="http://example.com/bpmn/supplier-onboarding">
  <bpmn:process id="Process_SupplierOnboarding" name="Supplier Selection and Onboarding" isExecutable="false">
    <bpmn:startEvent id="StartEvent_NeedIdentified" name="Need for new supplier identified">
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_1</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:startEvent>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_IssueRFP" name="Issue request for proposals (RFP)">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_1</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_2</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_ReceiveProposals" name="Receive supplier proposals">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_2</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_3</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_EvaluateProposals" name="Evaluate proposals (cost, quality, delivery time)">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_3</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_4</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_AssessmentSplit" name="Additional assessment required?" default="Flow_SkipAssessment">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_4</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_AssessmentYes</bpmn:outgoing>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_SkipAssessment</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:exclusiveGateway>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_SiteVisitsInterviews" name="Conduct site visits or interviews with suppliers">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_AssessmentYes</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_5</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_AssessmentJoin" name="Assessment complete">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_5</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_SkipAssessment</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_6</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:exclusiveGateway>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_SelectSupplier" name="Analyze proposals and select supplier">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_6</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_7</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_NegotiateContract" name="Negotiate contract terms">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_7</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_8</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_SignContract" name="Sign contract">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_8</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_9</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_OnboardSupplier" name="Onboard supplier and execute contract">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_9</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_10</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="EndEvent_Onboarded" name="Supplier onboarded and contract executed">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_10</bpmn:incoming>
    </bpmn:endEvent>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_1" sourceRef="StartEvent_NeedIdentified" targetRef="Task_IssueRFP" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_2" sourceRef="Task_IssueRFP" targetRef="Task_ReceiveProposals" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_3" sourceRef="Task_ReceiveProposals" targetRef="Task_EvaluateProposals" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_4" sourceRef="Task_EvaluateProposals" targetRef="Gateway_AssessmentSplit" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_AssessmentYes" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_AssessmentSplit" targetRef="Task_SiteVisitsInterviews" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_SkipAssessment" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_AssessmentSplit" targetRef="Gateway_AssessmentJoin" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_5" sourceRef="Task_SiteVisitsInterviews" targetRef="Gateway_AssessmentJoin" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_6" sourceRef="Gateway_AssessmentJoin" targetRef="Task_SelectSupplier" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_7" sourceRef="Task_SelectSupplier" targetRef="Task_NegotiateContract" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_8" sourceRef="Task_NegotiateContract" targetRef="Task_SignContract" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_9" sourceRef="Task_SignContract" targetRef="Task_OnboardSupplier" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_10" sourceRef="Task_OnboardSupplier" targetRef="EndEvent_Onboarded" />
  </bpmn:process>
</bpmn:definitions>

rules.instruction: When the description opens by saying that the process starts when a participant performs a named action (for example identifying a need), so that action is a performed step that precedes the first described activity: Model a plain start event with no label that carries the action. Add a task named for the participant's action, placed after the start event and before the first described activity. Route the sequence flow start event, then action task, then the first activity. Do not put the action into the start event's label, and do not drop the action because the trigger already implies it.
rules.situation: the description says the process begins when a participant performs a named opening action (such as identifying a need), so that action is a performed step that comes after the process starts

rules.instruction: When the description states that, after a document or agreement is signed or finalized, a further action follows it (for example, a party is set up or activated), and the process ends with that further action together with another outcome: Model each stated post-signing action as its own task placed after the signing task and connected to it by a sequence flow, in the order the description gives. Connect that task to the end event or to the final task, so the action is not skipped, and do not fold it into the signing task or the final task.
rules.situation: the description states that, after a document or agreement is signed or finalized, a further action follows it (for example, a party is set up or activated), and the process ends with that further action together with another outcome

rules.instruction: When the description joins two actions with 'and' in one clause, where one action is a selection or evaluation and the other is a follow-up that the description places after a separately stated step: Model the selection or evaluation and the follow-up it leads into as separate tasks, in the order the description gives, each labelled with its own verb-object phrase. Do not fold the follow-up into the selection task. Model any separately stated intermediate step as its own task between them.
rules.situation: the description joins two actions with 'and' in one clause, where one action is a selection or evaluation and the other is a follow-up that the description places after a separately stated step

rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity is optional (for example with 'may also') and places it between two steps that are otherwise required in sequence: Model the optional activity as a task reached from an exclusive decision gateway, with a bypass flow from that same gateway. Join the activity path and the bypass path with one exclusive merge placed before the next required step. Keep every required step in the order the description gives, on the main path. The bypass must not skip a required step that comes before the next decision point.
rules.situation: the description states that an activity is optional (for example with 'may also') and places it between two steps that are otherwise required in sequence

promoted.trigger: the description states that, after a completing step is finished, a further action follows it (for example, a participant is configured or enabled), and the process ends with that further action together with another outcome
promoted.instruction: Model each stated follow-up action as its own task placed after the completing task and connected to it by a sequence flow, in the order the description gives. Connect that task to the end event or to the final task so the action is not skipped, and do not fold it into the completing task or the final task.
promoted.detail: general form of EXS-009, written after it improved the model of example 05
